topic: The Curious Link: Elastic Collisions and the Digits of Pi
target_audience: High school or undergraduate physics/math enthusiasts

sections.title: The Setup: The 1D Collision Paradox
lecture_lines: Consider two blocks on a frictionless surface.
Block B has mass one hundred to the n.
They collide elastically with a wall.
We count the total number of collisions.
animations: Fade in two circles with masses M and m.
Circle m moves towards M with velocity vector.
Flash collision point to emphasize impact.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Energy and momentum are both conserved.
The wall reverses the direction of velocity.
animations: Display formula for Momentum: p = mv.
Highlight variables p, v, E, m with #00FF00.

sections.title: The Mathematical Mapping: Phase Space
lecture_lines: Map collisions to geometry in phase space.
Collisions correspond to reflections off the ellipse.

sections.title: The Revelation: Connecting to Pi
lecture_lines: Large mass ratios reveal digits of pi.
One hundred ratio gives thirty-one collisions.
Ten thousand ratio gives three hundred fourteen.
The geometry matches the arctangent expansion.
Digits of pi appear in the collisions.
animations: Transform trajectory into a circular arc.
Overlay a circle arc with radius r.
Draw tangent line relative to arc.
Final flash of the Pi result.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
lecture_lines: Pi is hidden in velocity space geometry.
Blocks act as an analog computer.
animations: Fade in the final two blocks.
